listing.name: Rocket: Robot on Wheels (Rocket-R)
listing.summary: Play Rocket: Robot on Wheels with your own matching US game file.

steps.title: Select your own Rocket ROM on first Play
steps.instruction: On first Play, choose your own supported Rocket: Robot on Wheels US ROM in the upstream launcher. It verifies the game and remembers the chosen path. Use the upstream menus for controls and compatible mods; no game compilation or separate installer is needed for the published player.

steps.title: Keep saves and mod profiles separately backed up
steps.instruction: Default Windows saves, settings, mod profiles, mod-specific saves, logs and crash reports use %APPDATA%/Rocket-R. Keep a separate backup of the actual profile before changing versions; older versions may not read newer saves. Its external profile is outside Portcove backup and runtime rollback; rollback does not rewind saves. Keep each release’s own bundled engine/mod resources together, and keep custom --config or developer paths backed up separately.

steps.title: Choose the Linux package for your system
steps.instruction: Portcove manages the direct x86-64 AppImage. It needs working AppImage and FUSE support, glibc 2.35, GLIBCXX 3.4.30 and a Vulkan driver. For an external Linux copy, choose the matching x86-64 or ARM64 AppImage or follow the upstream Portable archive instructions. Steam Deck has a separate package and START-ROCKET-R.sh. You maintain those external copies.

steps.title: Open Rocket-R on Android
steps.instruction: Install the upstream ARM64 APK on Android 7 or later on a device with the required Vulkan 1.2 features. Choose your own matching US ROM in the app and keep the original separately. The app stores a private ROM copy and its own saves, settings and mod profiles. Preserve app data before clearing storage, uninstalling or changing packages. You update this Android installation yourself.

references.title: Check your original game file
references.instruction: Rocket-R accepts your own US game with code NSUE, 12 MiB and canonical SHA-1 622d71a44da0b81ea68092cac9198c66154a4f4a. The desktop launcher accepts .z64, .n64 and .v64 files.

references.title: Find your Linux profile and launch logs
references.instruction: By default the game uses $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/rocket-r or ~/.config/rocket-r for settings, saves and mod profiles. A custom --config path or the rocket-r-data fallback changes where you need to back up. The upstream launcher records logs in $XDG_STATE_HOME/rocket-r or ~/.local/state/rocket-r, with a temporary-directory fallback when needed.

presentation.manual_preparation: On first Play, choose your own supported Rocket: Robot on Wheels US ROM in the upstream launcher. It verifies the game and remembers the chosen path. Use the upstream menus for controls and compatible mods; no game compilation or separate installer is needed for the published player. Default Windows saves, settings, mod profiles, mod-specific saves, logs and crash reports use %APPDATA%/Rocket-R. Keep a separate backup of the actual profile before changing versions; older versions may not read newer saves. Portcove preserves only the declared rocket-r-data in-folder fallback for its managed Windows copy. Its external profile is outside Portcove backup and runtime rollback; rollback does not rewind saves. Keep each release’s own bundled engine/mod resources together, and keep custom --config or developer paths backed up separately. Existing external copies retain their files and runtime update owner. Managed Linux uses the direct x86-64 AppImage. Keep the Linux profile under $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/rocket-r or ~/.config/rocket-r outside the runtime and backed up separately. Use a separate copy for an adjacent AppImage profile or a custom launch.
